body: Aside from the `ul` stuff, lgtm

Update: `<li>`s-outside-`<ol>`s are crazypants. http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/?saved=4640 is my latest foray. Time for some code inspection into Blink to see if we can salvage a usable algorithm here...
This still matches what I said in [this comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/2002#discussion_r86054502) that `<li>`s share a same counter when they have the same parent element.

Yeah. Currently I'm in https://cs.chromium.org/chromium/src/third_party/WebKit/Source/core/layout/LayoutListItem.cpp?sq=package:chromium&rcl=1478101093&l=516 which does indeed appear to just pick the parent element if not inside an `<ol>`. <del>(Note: no special casing for `<ul>`.)</del> <ins>Wrong, it does count `<ul>`</ins>

I'm now trying to figure out how Chromium calculates the numbering. I also want to see if the menu, ol, ul, li, dir reset rule applies for them. I guess we also need to write tests for that.

One note that, if you are going to scope on the parent element, please ensure to scope on "an ancestor element which generates a box" or something similiar instead. Otherwise it would be tricky for any engine which supports `display: contents` (Gecko is the only browser does that as far as I know, though). There is [something simliar](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/#counters-without-boxes) for CSS's `counter()` as well.
OK. Can I count on your help writing web platform tests for that kind of case?
Yeah. I can add a test for `display: contents` thing (although no browser would be able to pass that test at the moment).

Alright, take 2 up and ready for review. This matches Chrome/WebKit for cases like http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/?saved=4646 and http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/?saved=4647, instead of Edge/Firefox, since it seemed a bit simpler and Edge/Firefox disagree on the second of those links. Let me know what you think.

If we think this sounds reasonable, I'll write tests tomorrow.

Firefox has fixed the second case to align with WebKit's behavior.

I think making the first case match WebKit/Blink is unreasonable, because they do not support `<menu>` according to the caniuse panel. I think `<menu>` should be able to own `<li>`s.
That makes sense, will fix.
Give me some time to think about the list owner algorithm. I guess the current algorithm isn't very friendly to Gecko's current impl.

It seems to me that we may need to consider a bit deeper about how this should interact with [CSS Lists spec](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/). I think in the world CSS Lists spec describes, `ol`, `ul`, `li` can be implemented using some CSS presentational hints via `counter()` function and `counter-*` properties (with some magic for starting value of `<ol reverse>`, though).

In that world, `li`s which are not scoped by any list would share a global counter. But that doesn't match any of current impls, and that could potentially be terrible for performance.

I guess that is a fundamental issue from the design of `counter()`, and is probably unresolvable there. But I don't want the world describes by HTML spec conflicts with that from the CSS spec... I have no idea.

@tabatkins, do you have any idea about the interaction between the two specs around list items which are not scoped by a list?

Yeah, I was looking at that spec. What I'd be interested in knowing is whether any implementers have near-term plans to replace their current list item counter creation code with a CSS based solution. I assumed not, so I went ahead and specified this, but I'd welcome finding out I'm wrong. Also cc @tabatkins as he's the editor.

I don't think any browser has that plan in near-term. I just think we need to take that into account before we decide what we want. If we want the behavior specified here, we should probably make it clear in that the CSS spec that it is infeasible to implement the behavior in CSS.

Yeah, I'm less interested in coming up with an ideal "what we want" behavior, than I am in driving everyone toward interop, and in producing something that new engines can use to achieve compatibility with existing content. In other words, I'm interested in a solution that matches existing browsers in all cases where there is majority agreement, and in picking the simplest among alternatives when there are conflicts.

That said, I'm not opposed to coming up with and speccing some ideal behavior in the future, if enough implementer interest materializes. But near-term my priority is to get something closer to reality than the current spec.

OK, this algorithm looks fine to me, although Gecko may need some nontrivial code change to match that behavior, which we probably don't have plan to do at the moment. I'll file a bug for that anyway.

I think `display: list-item` is out-of-scope for HTML spec... But now we have an issue that some part of the algorithm is defined in HTML spec, and the other part is defined in CSS spec... which sounds bad...

The question is, per the proposed spec text, when can something not have a list owner? As far as I can tell, it is only if it's an `<li>` with no ancestors that generate CSS boxes. I guess this is technically possible, if you `display: contents` everything except the `<li>`? @upsuper, how should that work?

> We also have to deal with display: list-item elements (http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/saved/4651)

Fair point. I think we can do this. We just expand the list of elements from being li elements, to being elements whose computed value of display is list-item. http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/?saved=4652 seems to support this.

There's precedent for this kind of computed-style-dependent stuff in https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-innertext-idl-attribute.
I guess just let it not have list owner is fine if that really happens... I don't think we need to care a lot about that kind of edge cases...

OK, tests up at https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/pull/4169, and spec should be ready for editor review. Thanks everyone for your help along this fun journey!

> @tabatkins, do you have any idea about the interaction between the two specs around list items which are not scoped by a list?

The Lists spec is complex, but very clear, about how counters work; there's no such thing as a "list" in the model.

Implementations' treatments of `<li>` and `list-item` are just nonsense that works fine for the traditional use-case (`<li>` in a list container) but have unpredictable behavior outside of that, because they didn't care about those cases, so you just get some arbitrary behavior that falls out of the implementation details.  They're optimized for better speed, because CSS counters can be a little slow, but people sometimes use enormous lists and expect them to work quickly.

If browsers are interested in having their implementations make more sense, great. I'd love to see that specced well; in an ideal world this is reflected in CSS concepts, perhaps new ones - I've talked with @esprehn before about having an alternate counter concept that works more simply/quickly for use with HTML lists.  But absent that, I'm pessimistic about ever having it adequately explained in the CSS world.
